title: Fragment breadcrumbs: trace mapping and streaming content scrub playbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Provide a robust, low-overhead observability playbook for streaming API responses that maps per-fragment (incremental output) metrics to tracing spans while ensuring deterministic redaction of PII in logs and telemetry. This ticket defines the telemetry schema, trace stitching strategy, deterministic scrub rules, and rollout plan across the hosted API, Dedicated, and Private runtimes.

Scope:
- Instrument the runtime to emit lightweight 'fragment.breadcrumb' events for each incremental send (append/replace events) with stable fragment ids.
- Attach or reference a short-lived fragment_id to trace spans so that traces can be joined with fragment metrics without leaking content.
- Implement deterministic scrub hooks for loggers and observability exporters so raw fragments never land in logs or APM backends.
- Define sampling and retention policy: full traces only for error cases; aggregated per-fragment histograms for latency and token counts retained at high cardinality; content-level metrics aggregated only by safe buckets.

Why different from prior work: previous tickets focused on chunk-level metrics and heuristics for sampling. This playbook emphasizes an explicit breadcrumb abstraction (fragment_id, ordinal, parent_request_id, tool_call_context) and a deterministic redaction pipeline that is shared by tracing, logs, and metrics exporters. It's also explicitly compatibility-aware for older API clients that use the incremental 'choice' protocol and for new structured-output flows (function/tool calling).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits 'fragment.breadcrumb' event for every sent fragment with fields: fragment_id, ordinal, request_id, length_tokens, latency_ms_bucket, tool_context (optional)
Tracing: each fragment event is associated with a span_id or referenced via fragment_id; trace queries can return list of fragment ordinals for a request within 5s of completion
Redaction: raw fragment content is never sent to external telemetry backends; sanitized fingerprints (HMAC) can be attached for de-dup/diagnostics without revealing content
Dashboards: per-request fragment latency histogram, per-model median fragment size, and tool-call failure rate by fragment are visible in Grafana
Compatibility: behavior degrades gracefully for clients using older streaming protocols (fallback to aggregated chunk metrics)
tasks: Design: finalize breadcrumb event schema and proto (obs.team + infra) - deliver design doc
Runtime: instrument send path to emit breadcrumb events and attach fragment_id to trace context
Tracing: add span linker util that maps fragment_id -> span and exposes fast query index
Redaction: implement deterministic scrub pipeline that runs before any telemetry export; add HMAC fingerprinting for fragments
Metrics: update dogfood dashboards and create aggregation jobs for per-fragment latency and size
Compatibility shim: detect older clients and emit aggregated chunk metrics instead of breadcrumbs
E2E tests: create integration tests for trace linkage, sampling behavior, and redaction checkpoints
Rollout: staged rollout plan across hosted -> dedicated -> private with feature flag and telemetry validation
notes: Decision: use a stable 128-bit fragment_id generated from request_id + ordinal to avoid new datastore writes per-fragment; this keeps breadcrumb events purely append-only
Trade-off: attaching fragment_id to trace context increases span trace size marginally; mitigated by keeping fragment payloads out of span attributes and only attaching HMAC fingerprints
Privacy: we will NOT attach any raw text to telemetry. For debugging, dev tiers can opt-in to ephemeral debug blobs stored in a customer-only, access-controlled bucket (separate ticket).
Sampling policy: errors and tool-call failures -> 100% trace retention for N hours; successful flows -> 0.5% sampling by request, plus aggregation of all fragment histograms at service-level
Compatibility detail: older clients send 'delta' envelopes without tool_context; breadcrumb schema includes optional tool_context so consumers can unify both paths
QA_steps: Run integration harness that simulates streaming with nested tool calls and verify fragment_id continuity across tool boundaries
Confirm Grafana dashboards show expected latency spikes when injecting artificial backpressure in runtime
Run log exporter with redaction enabled; audit that no fragment text appears in any telemetry sinks using automated grep across backends
Verify that the aggregated histograms match raw per-fragment measurements within 0.5% in a controlled load test
